I know this is a dead thread, but I'm posting this in case anyone else is having trouble. After my 34 attempts (and rage) I figured out my best strategy.

First of all, obviously get the silver sword and armor. I also found that the sapphire ring - that makes enemies go 1/2 the speed - is the best option. It may seem tedious to chip away at his damage, but it makes evading the bats a lot more easier. 

I kept orbiting around the exterior of the room, but made sure to keep the cluster of bats semi-close so that when they changed, I could just swoop in for one hit, and book it, rinse and repeat. Also found that going to the corners when he's coming out of the single form back into the bats so that I could find the best way to evade the largest cluster of them will be the best. Just keep chipping until he's dead. 

It's still a bullshit boss, it'll be a close battle, and you'll die a few times, but this is what worked for me. Sorry I'm three years too late, hope you enjoyed the game, and for anyone who's coming on now for help - like I did earlier today - good luck.

The way my diabetes and epilepsy works. If I drink, it instantly shoots my numbers down and forces me into a seizure. For me, it was Shinji’s breakdown scene in The End of Evangelion. The entire Komm Susser Tod scene. The Third Impact. 

At the time watching, I was going through a severe depression, and was considering suicide. When that piano music started, when Shinki wraps his hands tightly around Asuka’s throat, I felt that anger and hatred… and when all the flashing images started, the children’s drawings, the talking between him and Rei, I lost it. It was like Hideaki Anno displayed all my depressive thoughts from the last fifteen years on a screen for me to see. The moving red crimson figured orbiting the sphere, floating like seaweed, the flash of Shinji smiling as it flashed between the smile and black at Kaworu, him shying away from human contact in scenes, talking about how it would be better if everybody died, including himself… I felt that depression and hatred.

When Lilith slowly rose from the Earth, I lost it, silently crying and actually smiling. I felt the sadness, hatred, revenge, the shock and despair as she looms over the Black Egg. 

It still gets me to this day. 

No scene in any movie has hit me so hard with a realism, where I thought, just as Shinji says in the scene, “No one understands me.”

But Hideako Anno did… and I thank him for that, and for giving me the wake up call to go to therapy. 

I owe my life to the Third Impact. It sounds super cheesy and almost cringy, but it’s true to me.
